description: This dataset gives, for every day since March 2020, how many COVID-19 patients were in Czech hospitals and how much intensive care they needed, one of the longest open national series of pandemic hospital load. It is published by the Czech Ministry of Health on its Onemocnění aktuálně portal, built with the Institute of Health Information and Statistics (ÚZIS) and Masaryk University, from the National Health Information System. Each daily row gives newly admitted and cumulative patients, the number in hospital, their split by severity (no symptoms, mild, moderate, severe), and the numbers in intensive care, on oxygen, on high-flow oxygen, on mechanical ventilation and on ECMO, with deaths. The file is available as a free download in CSV and JSON and is still updated daily. Caveats: figures are national only in the open file (regional aggregates sit in an authorised-access section), the series covers COVID-19 patients, not total bed occupancy, and definitions of severity follow the Czech reporting system. Simulation uses: calibrating epidemic hospital demand models, testing intensive care surge capacity, and comparing waves against capacity limits. Related records: the California county hospital capacity data (data-california-covid19-hospital-capacity-by-county) and the French COVID hospital incidence data (data-france-covid-hospital-incidence-contact-networks) are comparable series.
